violin.definition: Bowed stringed instrument that is the highest member of the violin family.
violin.exampleUsage: The violin played the upper melody in the ensemble.

viola.definition: A bowed string instrument, larger and lower-pitched than a violin.
viola.exampleUsage: The viola supplied a lower string part.

cello.exampleUsage: The seated player supported the cello between the knees.

double-bass.definition: The largest and lowest-pitched common member of the orchestral string family.
double-bass.exampleUsage: The double bass supplied the lowest part in the string section.

harp.definition: A large string instrument played by plucking its strings.
harp.exampleUsage: The musician plucked the harp's strings.

guitar.definition: A stringed instrument usually having six strings.
guitar.exampleUsage: The musician played a chord on the guitar.

bow.definition: A stick strung with hair that is drawn across strings to produce sound.
bow.exampleUsage: The player drew the bow across the strings.

string.definition: A stretched cord or wire on an instrument that vibrates to produce a note.
string.exampleUsage: The string vibrated to produce the note.

tuning-peg.definition: A small peg or mechanism turned to adjust the tension and pitch of a musical instrument string.
tuning-peg.exampleUsage: The tuning peg adjusts the string's tension.

chin-rest.definition: A fitted support that lets a violinist rest the chin while holding and playing the instrument.
chin-rest.exampleUsage: The chin rest supports the violinist's chin.

flute.exampleUsage: The flute played the bright upper passage.

clarinet.definition: A single-reed instrument with a straight tube.
clarinet.exampleUsage: The clarinet uses a single reed.

oboe.exampleUsage: The oboe uses a double reed.

bassoon.definition: A long, low-pitched woodwind instrument played with a double reed.
bassoon.exampleUsage: The bassoon played the lower woodwind phrase.

piccolo.definition: A small flute that makes very high notes.
piccolo.exampleUsage: The piccolo sounded above the other flutes in this passage.

recorder.definition: A woodwind instrument blown through a mouthpiece and played using finger holes.
recorder.exampleUsage: The player covered the recorder's finger holes.

saxophone.definition: A single-reed woodwind with a conical bore.
saxophone.exampleUsage: The saxophone joined the ensemble for the arranged piece.

reed.definition: A vibrator consisting of a thin strip of stiff material that vibrates to produce a tone when air streams over it.
reed.exampleUsage: The reed vibrates when air passes over it.

mouthpiece.definition: The part of a wind instrument through which the player directs air.
mouthpiece.exampleUsage: The player directs air through the mouthpiece.

key.definition: A lever pressed to produce or control a note on an instrument.
key.exampleUsage: The key controls an opening on the wind instrument.

trumpet.definition: A brass instrument usually played using three valves to change notes.
trumpet.exampleUsage: The trumpet played the brass melody.

trombone.definition: A brass instrument consisting of a long tube whose length can be varied by a U-shaped slide.
trombone.exampleUsage: The trombone's slide changes the tube length.

french-horn.definition: A brass instrument has a gradually widening tube wound into a spiral, with valves that alter the notes.
french-horn.exampleUsage: The French horn played the sustained orchestral phrase.

tuba.exampleUsage: The tuba supplied the low brass part.

cornet.definition: A brass musical instrument with a brilliant tone.
cornet.exampleUsage: The cornet played the melody in the brass band.

bugle.definition: A simple brass instrument often used to play military calls.
bugle.exampleUsage: The bugle sounded the specified call.

valve.definition: A mechanism on a brass instrument that changes the route of air to alter pitch.
valve.exampleUsage: The valve changes the route of air through the instrument.

bell.definition: The flared opening at the end of a wind instrument.
bell.exampleUsage: The bell forms the flared opening at the instrument's end.

mute.definition: A device used to change or reduce the sound of a musical instrument.
mute.exampleUsage: The mute modifies the instrument's sound.

slide.definition: The movable section of a trombone used to change the length of its air tube.
slide.exampleUsage: The trombone player moved the slide during the phrase.

drum.exampleUsage: The player struck the drum's membrane.
drum.definition: A percussion instrument played by striking a stretched surface.

snare-drum.definition: A shallow drum has tightly stretched heads and wires held against the lower head. Striking it produces a sharp, rattling sound.
snare-drum.exampleUsage: The snare drum produced a rattling effect through its wires.

bass-drum.definition: A large percussion instrument with two heads produces a deep, indefinite-pitched sound.
bass-drum.exampleUsage: The bass drum supplied the deep percussion sound.

timpani.definition: Kettledrums with adjustable pitch, commonly used in an orchestra.
timpani.exampleUsage: The timpani were tuned for the orchestral passage.

cymbal.definition: A percussion instrument consisting of a concave brass disk.
cymbal.exampleUsage: The player struck the cymbal to produce the accent.

triangle.definition: A metal percussion instrument shaped as a triangle and struck with a metal beater.
triangle.exampleUsage: The triangle sounded when struck with its beater.

xylophone.definition: A percussion instrument with wooden bars tuned to produce a chromatic scale and with resonators.
xylophone.exampleUsage: The xylophone has tuned wooden bars.

tambourine.definition: A shallow drum with a single drumhead and with metallic disks in the sides.
tambourine.exampleUsage: The tambourine's jingles sounded during the rhythm.

gong.definition: A percussion instrument consisting of a metal plate that is struck with a softheaded drumstick.
gong.exampleUsage: The player struck the gong for the resonant accent.

drumstick.definition: A stick used to strike a drum or another percussion instrument.
drumstick.exampleUsage: The drumstick is used to strike the percussion instrument.

concert-hall.definition: A building or room designed for live musical performances.
concert-hall.exampleUsage: The concert hall provides the performance space.

stage.definition: A raised area where musicians or other performers appear before an audience.
stage.exampleUsage: The musicians took their places on the stage.

music-stand.definition: A lightweight support keeps pages of written music open and visible while someone plays.
music-stand.exampleUsage: The music stand held the player's score.

conductor-s-podium.definition: A small raised platform on which an orchestra conductor stands so musicians can see the conducting gestures.
conductor-s-podium.exampleUsage: The conductor's podium raised the conductor above the surrounding floor.

baton.definition: A thin tapered rod used by a conductor to lead an orchestra or choir.
baton.exampleUsage: The conductor used a baton to indicate the musical pulse.

sheet-music.definition: A visual record of a musical work shows performers its notes, rhythms, volume changes, and other instructions.
sheet-music.exampleUsage: The musician read the sheet music before rehearsal.

score.definition: Written music showing the parts played or sung in a piece.
score.exampleUsage: The score shows the work's instrumental parts.

tuning-fork.definition: A metal tool with two prongs produces a steady pitch when struck and helps musicians tune their instruments.
tuning-fork.exampleUsage: The tuning fork provides a reference pitch.

metronome.definition: A device providing a regular pulse to mark a musical tempo.
metronome.exampleUsage: The metronome marked a regular pulse during practice.

orchestra-pit.definition: A lowered area in front of a stage where an orchestra plays.
orchestra-pit.exampleUsage: The orchestra pit holds musicians below the front of the stage.

conductor.definition: A person who directs musicians during rehearsal or performance.

concertmaster.definition: A principal violinist leads the first violin section, connects the players with the conductor, tunes the orchestra, and coordinates bowing, phrasing, and cues.
concertmaster.exampleUsage: The concertmaster led the first violin section.

soloist.definition: A musician who performs a solo.
soloist.exampleUsage: The soloist performed the featured passage.

first-chair.definition: The leading player in a section of an orchestra, usually seated closest to the conductor.
first-chair.exampleUsage: The first-chair player led the instrumental section.

section-leader.definition: The principal musician responsible for leading a particular instrumental section.
section-leader.exampleUsage: The section leader explained the phrasing to the players.

accompanist.definition: A person who provides musical accompaniment (usually on a piano).
accompanist.exampleUsage: The accompanist supported the solo performer's part.

composer.definition: A person who composes music, usually as a profession.

arranger.definition: A musician who adapts a piece of music for particular instruments or voices.
arranger.exampleUsage: The arranger adapted the work for the selected instruments.

page-turner.definition: A person who turns the pages of printed music for a performer whose hands are occupied playing.
page-turner.exampleUsage: The page turner turned the pianist's score pages.

audience.definition: A gathering of spectators or listeners at a (usually public) performance.
audience.exampleUsage: The audience listened to the concert.

podium.definition: A platform raised above the surrounding level to give prominence to the person on it.
podium.exampleUsage: The conductor stepped onto the podium.

symphony.definition: A substantial orchestral work, often organized in several movements.

rehearsal.definition: A practice session in preparation for a public performance (as of a play or speech or concert).
rehearsal.exampleUsage: The rehearsal prepared the ensemble for the concert.

program.definition: A printed or digital list of works and performers in a concert.
program.exampleUsage: The program lists the works and performers.
